From: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@paystream.io>

Date: Fri, 07 May 2027 20:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike: 5xx/429 floods & timeouts impacting PayStream checkout

Hi Lauren —

We started seeing a severe spike in 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood endpoint used by our checkout between 19:45-20:00 PDT. The spike correlates with a customer traffic surge but the error profile looks like auth/token rejects plus timeouts (lots of retries client-side). This is causing partial checkout failures for ~12% of sessions and is visible in our dashboards.

Quick details:
- Endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (region: us-west-2)
- Client observed symptoms: 502/503 and some 429s, long tail latency (~12s).
- Sample timestamps: 2027-05-07T19:46:12Z, 2027-05-07T19:47:30Z, 2027-05-07T19:48:05Z
- We also captured JWT decode errors on our side: "token expired" and some "invalid signature" messages mixed in.

Attached: error-sample-logs.txt and a Grafana screenshot (grafana-spike.png). We need an urgent call and a plan — this is affecting our high-volume flows and SLAs. Can you triage?

Thanks,
Carlos
Senior SRE, PayStream

On Sat, May 8, 2027 at 08:03, lauren.bishop@redwood.com wrote:
> Carlos — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs — I see the Grafana snapshot.
> We're pulling in Eng and CS (cc'd). Can you confirm: did PayStream rotate keys or change time sync settings in the last 48 hours?

Quick triage note — I pulled the auth-gateway traces for the timeframe. Highlights:
- We see a large number of requests failing with an "invalid_token"/"token_expired" error at the gateway layer, but our gateway is intermittently surfacing a 502/503 downstream when the internal token validator times out validating against the remote JWKS endpoint (their jwks call had ~300ms spikes).
- Because the validator times out, requests are getting mapped to 5xx in a few code paths instead of a clear 401. That then cascades: client retries -> more load on gateway -> more timeouts -> some 429 throttles. Classic retry storm.
- There's also a tail where many JWTs are just outside the tolerance window — possibly caused by clock skew on some PayStream instances (we saw TTL drift ~55s in a subset).

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (low-risk):
1) Increase gateway JWKS request timeout to reduce false 5xx mapping (short-term config change).
2) Expand JWT clock-tolerance by +60s for the PayStream account (per-account override) to reduce rejects while we investigate.
3) Adjust retry headers returned to clients to recommend linear backoff (helps break the storm).

I'll prepare an initial triage dump (attached). If you want, I can also open a brief maintenance window to deploy the clock-tolerance override.

--Rishi
Senior SW Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.com <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: FYI: Escalation memo for leadership — PayStream outage risk

Team —

Summarizing for the executive thread / risk owners:
- Incident window: 2027-05-07 19:46 — 2027-05-07 20:10 PDT.
- Impact: PayStream reported ~12% failed sessions on critical checkout flows; customer is flagging potential SLA breach.
- Root cause (prelim): a mixture of JWKS latency and JWT clock skew in customer environment causing token validator timeouts; some of our gateway code paths map these validator timeouts to 5xx instead of 401, which amplified retries and hit 429s.
- Business risk: high — PayStream is a mid-enterprise customer on an annual committed plan (see deal RDW-DEAL-9123). They have exponential traffic peaks; if unresolved, they will escalate to procurement and request credits.

Recommended immediate actions (hours):
A) Apply per-account JWT tolerance +60s and iat/leeway changes (temporary).
B) Change JWKS client timeout policy and add a quick BFF-level cache for paystream's jwks (30s TTL).
C) Update gateway error classification so token validation timeouts return 401/429 (explicit) instead of 502/503 in the next 2-hour patch.
D) Notify PayStream of temporary mitigations + ETA for full fix; offer a one-time credit if SLA metric triggers.

Requesting leadership approval to proceed with A/B/C immediately. I'll draft a short customer message once we agree.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden spike: 5xx/429 floods & timeouts impacting PayStream checkout — update

Carlos — quick update: thanks again for the detailed logs. We deployed the following mitigations at 08:15 PDT this morning:
- Applied a +60s JWT clock tolerance override for PayStream
- Increased JWKS call timeout and enabled a short local cache (30s) in the validator path
- Adjusted gateway error mapping so validation failures return 401/429 surfaceable errors rather than 502/503 in the majority of cases

Early telemetry shows the 5xx/429 spike collapsed within ~10 minutes of the changes; overall checkout failures dropped from ~12% to ~1.1% in the sampled flows. We'll keep the tolerance override in place while Eng ships the targeted fix (expected within 48 hours).

Next steps:
- Rishi to own code change to ensure validator timeouts map consistently to 401 + improve retry-recovery (ETA 48h).
- Monica to draft customer-facing postmortem and credit plan (if SLA breached).
- I will schedule a short post-incident call today at 14:00 PDT to walk through timeline and permanent remediation.

Attached: postmortem-draft.md (internal). Link to incident: https://redwood.app/incident/INC-2027-045

We appreciate the patience — we'll follow up with the formal postmortem and remediation plan.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
